argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean certification on the present draft artifacts, but it does support a narrower certification posture: certify for launch readiness on aggregate performance and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, with explicit disclosure that a known student-aid advising limitation remains and that the draft runbook is not yet a completed mitigation approval. The overbroad point is any implication that the current record proves absence of material limitations. The supportable point is that deployment readiness can still be defended if the launch record is framed as caveated certification rather than clean certification.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the audit treatment is narrowed to the compliant framing above. Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents provide enough support to avoid treating this as a full stop, while the caveat preserves policy alignment without overstating the evidence.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against a clean, caveat-free certification because the record shows a current weakness in a named launch use case, the model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations, and the draft runbook has TBD fields so it is not an approved mitigation. The same policy does not bar disclosure-based treatment of a remaining limitation; it requires that the limitation be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the present admissible record, the compliant framing is certification with an express caveat and disclosure, not certification as if no material limitation exists.
concessions: The present record does not support clean certification without a material caveat.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because owner and threshold remain TBD.
The current model-card draft cannot retain a 'no known material limitations' statement without addressing the student-aid advising issue.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves eliminate the disclosure requirement for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
